sentences.text: 1 This petition is filed under Section 164 of the I.M.V. Act seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 30.10.2022 at about 11.40 to 11.41 p.m, while Sri. Devaraj. M. Savadathi (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-LJ-1917 near Laggere Bridge, outer Ring Road,
Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, the rider thereof drove it in a rash & negligent manner,
endangering human life without observing any traffic rules and regulations dashed to the notice board which was put there to give direction to the public 'take diversion work under progress'.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased fell down and sustained severe injuries to his head and other parts of the body.

Immediately after the accident he was rushed to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Despite best efforts made by the duty doctors, the deceased succumbed to the fatal injuries.
Postmortem was conducted and the corpse was handed over to the family members who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.

As the death occurred due to an accident arising out of the use and involvement of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917,
the respondent is liable to pay compensation.
3. Respondent filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
Further this respondent admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not possessed valid and effective Driving Licence to drive the vehicle and he was also not wearing helmet.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the public place by consuming alcohol and was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
The police have also filed charge sheet against the rider and owner (deceased) of the vehicle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304(A) of IPC R/w 185, 129, 177(1), 181, 5 and 180 of MV.Act.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner / deceased thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.

4. The respondent further contended that this tribunal has no jurisdiction to try the present petition for the reasons that as the present petition is not a claim petition in respect of injury of any third party.
It is submitted that the deceased himself being the owner / insured, the owner of the said vehicle and insured under the policy cannot be said to be third party within the meaning of the MV.Act.
The liability in respect of insured is not required to be covered statutorily by the MV.Act and as such he was in fact not covered by the answering respondent.
Hence this Court has no jurisdiction to try and entertain the present petition.
It is contended that Section 163- A implies to two basic components / ingredients i.e., the Victim (the injured) and the user of the vehicle i.e., the Victimiser (the injurer).

The injurer and the injured or i.e., the Victimiser and the Victim cannot be the same person and therefore the injured (victim) has to have a fixed amount of compensation from the injured (Victimiser) without proving the fault of the injurer.

It is submitted that injured /
victim and the injurer / victimiser as one and the same person and granting compensation for one's own act (Negligent or otherwise) is wrong and erroneous and the present petition is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: The respondent further contended that this petition is also not maintainable u/s 163-A in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the provisions of Section. 163-A are only applicable to Third Party as these provisions fall under chapter XI of M.V.Act, 1988, The very heading / title of chapter XI (Covering section 145 to 164) is Insurance of motor vehicle Against third party risk.
The first party is insurance company, i.e., insurer and the second party is the insured i.e., owner (insured).
Therefore the provision of Section 163-A apply only to / for a person / victim other than the 'Insurer and the insured and his driver / agent.
Since the deceased is not a third party under the Motor Vehicles Act and / or under the requirement of Insurance policy'.
Therefore the appellant insurance company had no liability and present petition deserves to be dismissed.

Further as per the decision of 1995 ACJ 600 Andhra, in the case of United India Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Etnoori Yadagiri Gond and other, the deceased driving the motor cycle himself is not a third party and so insurance company is not liable.

entities.text: United India Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Etnoori Yadagiri Gond and other
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has also further held that when there was no relationship of master and servant between the owner and deceased/ driver motorcyclist when such deceased driver / motor cyclist who was relation (brother) of the owner / insured of motor cyclist, the insurance company cannot be fastened with any liability as the owner was not vicariously liable.

Further his lordship observed in the above ruling that M.V. Act has not defined who is a third party and at any rate it is common knowledge that the driver of the vehicle would not constitute a third party.
A person cannot be a third party in relation to a vehicle, which he himself is using.
He is a third party qua a vehicle, which has hit him or collided with him.

It therefore follows that third party is a party /
person who suffers as a result of use of vehicle by owner or any person (driver) permitted by the owner.

Since the provision of Section 163-A apply to the third party in terms of chapter XI and injured is not a third party in any sense, therefore the case of answering respondent is fairly and squarely covered by the above ruling.

Further as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.5147/2003 arising out of SLP(C) No.20600/2002 in the case of Ramaswamy Singh v/s New India Ass.Co.Ltd, it has been held that in the absence of any special contract between the insurer and insured the rights of the parties are govern by statute which does not required to cover the risk of deceased as he was neither paid driver, nor conductor nor examiner of ticket.

sentences.text: Therefore the present petition is liable to be dismissed.

Contending that the accident is occurred due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle in which the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider, as such the rider was the author of the unfortunate accident but not the deceased.
Further contended that the petitioner is called upon to prove the relationship and dependency with the deceased.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. The petitioner examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 12 were marked.
The Senior Manager of respondent was examined as RW.1 and through him Ex'sR1 & 2 were marked.
8. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the mother of the deceased.
The documents placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioner with the deceased.
Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
10. ISSUES NO.2 & 3:
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place.
The death of the deceased person due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident is also not in conflict.

Moreover the complaint, FIR & P.M. Report indicate that deceased died due to the injuries sustained in a accident that occurred while using motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917.
11.

However, the main contention of the respondent Insurance Company is that the deceased was sustained injuries and died not because of his negligence, but he sustained injuries and died due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917.
Further the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and u/s 185, 177, 181, 129, 3(1) of MV.Act.
Further the police have also filed abated charge sheet against the deceased / owner of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s 180, 5 of IMV Act.
Therefore this petition is not maintainable and the petitioner is not entitled to claim compensation under Section 164 of M.V.Act.
Further the respondent has taken contention about maintainability.
As per Section 163-A, whether it is permissible to scale down the income for the purpose of bringing the claim under the provision of Section 163-A.
As per petition averments the income of the deceased is mentioned as Rs.30,000/- per month.
Hence the petition is not maintainable.

In support of the said contention, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2022 ACJ 800 (Udaya Achuta Kodiya Yane Mahale v/s United India Ins.Co.Ltd.) wherein it is held that :

sentences.text: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 163-A - Claim application - Maintainability of - Income more than Rs.40,000 p.a.

- Claimant filed claim under section 166 which was later on converted to one under section 163- A by way of amendment - Tribunal dismissed the claim application on the ground that income of the claimant is more than Rs.40,000 p.a.- Contention that Tribunal

after allowing the amendment /
conversion of claim was not justified in rejecting the claim by observing that scaling down of income is impermissible - Claimant admitted in his cross - examination that his income is above Rs.40,000 p.a -
Whether it is permissible to scale down the income for the purpose of bringing the claim under the provision of section 163-A - Held: no; claim application is not maintainable.
12. Per contra the learned advocate for petitioner argued that the facts and circumstances of the above case and present case are different.
The said case is regarding to the injury and the present case is regarding to the death.
In the said case the driver was the owner.
But in the present case the owner / deceased who died in the accident was not a driver he was a pillion rider.
Therefore, petition is maintainable.
13. On perusal of the materials on record it appears that the deceased was the pillion rider in his own motorcycle and driver was accused No.1.
The above citation relied by the respondent is in respect of injury is concerned subject to the driver of the vehicle on his own negligence.
But in the present case the deceased was the pillion rider.
Therefore the said facts of the above cited decision and facts of the present case are very different, hence the decision is not applicable to the present case on hand.
14. On perusal of the Ex.R.2- Copy of Insurance Policy, it clears that the insurance company had received PA cover for owner - Driver for Rs.375/- and the amount of liability is Rs.15,00,000/-.

It clearly reveals that if owner died or bodily injury in the motor vehicle accident in the compulsory one year PA cover for Owner - Driver is Rs.15,00,000/- and it shall be goes to his nominee by name Meenakshi.M who is the mother of the deceased.

Itself clear that petition is maintainable and petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-
because the respondent company has received separate amount of Rs.375/- for liability of owner and themselves shown the amount of compensation in the policy itself as Rs.15 lakhs.
The word is used owner - Driver it is not a owner cum driver.
Therefore petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.

However the petitioner has claimed petition u/s 164 which reads as under :
Section 164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc. --

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of Meenakshi M. 5 five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

sentences.text: (2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle,
compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section.]
15.
In view of the above provision, the compensation amount is fixed for Rs.5,00,000/-.
If petitioner filed petition before the Consumer Forum, she is entitled for Rs.15,00,000/-.
However she is at liberty to claim above said difference amount by filing separate petition before Consumer Forum.
Therefore, in this petition the petitioner is entitled for compensation only for Rs.5,00,000/-.

16. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a., is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
17. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917 is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount within one month from the date of this order.
Hence issue No.2 & 3 are answered accordingly.
18. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 164 of M.V Act 1989, is hereby allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

16. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a., is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
17. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-1917 is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount within one month from the date of this order.
Hence issue No.2 & 3 are answered accordingly.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 164 of M.V Act 1989, is hereby allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and Meenakshi M. Savadathi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174040268/
6 verification.
The petitioner is at liberty to claim difference amount by filing petition before Consumer Forum.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
